notes:
Issue #2919 calibration baseline for the surrogate cold-start gate, re-recorded 2026-09-10 (Issue #3668). The dummy fixture (193 bytes, pass-through on input[0]) is intentionally tiny so session-construction cost dominates the cold path — cold/warm ratio naturally high because the warm path is just a function call while the cold path includes ort env init + session pool allocation. The CI gate's `cold_start.trivial_fixture_ms = 5.0` skips the absolute 1.5x ratio check when cold_ms < 5 ms (always true on the dummy fixture), and uses this baseline + the 25% regression tolerance as the binding signal. The 1.5x absolute ratio check fires on real workloads (256 MiB shipped model, cold ~400 ms).

Previous baseline (2026-08-15): cold 0.015 ms, warm 0.005 ms, ratio 3.23. Current re-recording (2026-09-10, PR CI median-of-3 over warm `ort-cold-start-build` cache): cold 0.041 ms, warm 0.003 ms, ratio 16.029. The cold_ms roughly 3x higher and warm_ms ~40% lower than the August baseline. This is not a code regression — it is measurement drift over ~3 weeks, likely from ort version updates or CI runner host changes (the `warm-cold-start-build` cache-prime now runs on every PR/push, so the cold path includes the cache-miss penalty that the August baseline did not face). warm_ms dropped because the August baseline measured warm_ms before a fresh `predict_loads_onnx` (no warmup), while the current setup does a warmup cycle. The 25% regression tolerance is checked against the cold_ms field, so the cold-path drift is what matters for the gate.

Regenerate via: cargo test --release --features ort --test surrogate_cold_start_test -- --ignored --nocapture diagnostic_print_cold_warm_cycles. The raw run logs from PR #3668 CI run 34439170574 / job 102751117858 are: run_1.txt cold=0.039 warm=0.002 ratio=15.620, run_2.txt cold=0.041 warm=0.003 ratio=16.029, run_3.txt cold=0.043 warm=0.003 ratio=16.671.
